title: withWorkerPool requires real Postgres and worker-importable document-model sources, enforced at build time
content:
The executor worker pool moves job execution off the main thread into N `node:worker_threads` workers. Each worker opens its own Postgres pool and runs document models in isolation. Jobs route to a worker **stickily by document id**, so all work for one document lands on the same worker — which is how per-document serialization survives the move to multiple threads.

Calling `withWorkerPool` is what enables it; there is no `enabled` flag.

```typescript
const reactor = await new ReactorBuilder()
  .withDocumentModelSources([
    { packageName: "@my-org/account-document-model", subpath: "document-models" },
  ])
  .withWorkerPool({ numWorkers: 4, db: { host: "localhost", port: 5432, /* ... */ } })
  .build();
```

Two hard requirements, and the notable thing is that both are enforced up front rather than at runtime.

**Importable sources.** Workers re-import document models across the thread boundary, so a live module object cannot cross. Models must be registered as `{ filePath }` or `{ packageName }` sources. `buildModule()` throws on violation: `"withWorkerPool requires at least one worker-importable document-model source ({ filePath } or { packageName })."`, and for a model registered only as a live module, `"withWorkerPool requires worker-importable sources, but these models were registered only as live modules: ..."`. A live module for the same `documentType@version` may coexist as long as an importable source covers it. Sources resolve in one pass — file and package sources are imported host-side and their exports scanned for `DocumentModelModule` values — so host and workers are derived from the same list and cannot diverge.

**Real Postgres.** PGlite cannot be shared across threads, so parent and workers must point at the same Postgres instance. When the pool carries a `db`, the builder builds the parent's database from that same config unless `withKysely` overrides it.

Connection info, by contrast, is a *compile-time* guarantee: `WorkerPoolOptions` is a union requiring either `db` or a custom `factory`, making an enabled pool without connection info unrepresentable. `DbConfig` crosses worker IPC so it must be JSON-clonable; `ssl: true` maps to `{ rejectUnauthorized: false }`, `poolSize` to pg's `max`. The optional `verifier` is off by default — omit it and workers perform no executor-side signature verification, matching the in-process executor.

_Source: apps/academy/docs/academy/04-Reference/01-Reactor/07-StorageAndScaling.md (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45)._
